Resource:numberOfRecords.description: Use to indicate the total number of records in the dataset. This helps users understand the volume of data available and assess its suitability for specific types of analysis or research. Provide the total count of records, or an approximate average if the exact number is not available. This value reflects the total entries in the dataset, such as consultations, prescriptions, lab results, hospital admissions, etc. depending on the dataset's structure and content. This complements "number of unique individuals", which refers to how many distinct persons are represented in the dataset. Number of records refers to how many total data entries are available. For example, 10,000 individuals may each have multiple medical records, resulting in 100,000 total records
Resource:numberOfUniqueIndividuals.descr: Use this to indicate the number of unique individuals represented in the dataset. This provides users with a sense of the dataset's scale and its potential value for secondary use. This number should reflect the total (or approximate) count of distinct individuals whose data is included, helping potential data users quickly understand whether the dataset meets the scale requirements for their analysis or research purposes
Resource:populationCoverage.description: Indication of which part or group of the population is the subject of the data collection, e.g. infants aged 1 to 3 years or patients with type 2 diabetes
